_what: Allocation ceilings for the nightly benchmark job. Bytes allocated per operation, which is a property of the code rather than of the machine - so a shared runner measures the same figure this file was written from. See ADR-0023.
_gated: Allocation only. Timings are recorded to the job's artifacts and gated by nothing, because a timing threshold on a hosted runner fails for reasons nobody can act on.
_measuredWith: dotnet run --project bench/Spark.Benchmarks --configuration Release -- --filter '*' --exporters json --job short
_measuredOn: 2026-08-28, .NET 10, win-x64. Regenerate with the same --job short the nightly uses. That is for consistency, not to correct a known difference: the four EvaluationBenchmarks cases were measured under both the default and short configs and came back byte-identical.
_addingABenchmark: Add its entry here in the same change. The nightly FAILS on a benchmark with no baseline entry, deliberately: one running unguarded is a number nobody is watching.
_zeroIsAGuard: SceneIndexBenchmarks.Cull and HitTest are 0 and a 5% tolerance of 0 is 0, so any allocation at all on the cull path fails the job. That is intended - ADR-0013's bet is that culling a few thousand rectangles per frame is cheap, and an allocation per frame is how that stops being true.
